He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]]. ==Early life== Molinar grew up in [[Panama City]], Panama.{{cite web |last1=Horka |first1=Tyler |title='Panamanian Prince': How Iverson Molinar made it to Mississippi State |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2019/12/13/ncaa-college-basketball-mississippi-state-ben-howland-iverson-molinar-recruiting-panama/4348149002/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=December 13, 2019}} He moved to the United States at age 15 to play for [[Oaks Christian School]] in [[Westlake Village, California]].{{cite web |last1=Zaldivar |first1=Gabe |title=Veritas Prep Is Reshaping American Basketball With Latino Flavor |url=https://www.si.com/enfuego/news/veritas-prep-is-bringing-latin-america-to-us-basketball |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=July 8, 2020}} As a junior at Covenant Christian Ministries Academy in [[Marietta, Georgia]], Molinar averaged 21.5 points, six rebounds and five assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Lowery |first1=Logan |title=MSU adds commitment from Molinar |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/msu-adds-commitment-from-molinar/article_cef8a15e-8322-5337-84e5-eafa642a5481.html |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=October 23, 2018}} He played for Veritas National Prep School as a senior. Molinar also competed for Team Why Not, an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] program founded by NBA player [[Russell Westbrook]].{{cite web |last1=Lowery |first1=Logan |title=Molinar made his own way to MSU |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/college/molinar-made-his-own-way-to-msu/article_48cc62ad-8cf9-5377-b675-25078dc66fa7.html |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=February 7, 2020}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], among others. ==College career== On November 21, 2019, Molinar scored a freshman season-high 21 points in an 80–66 win over [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]].{{cite web |title=Iverson Molinar, Mississippi State cruise past Tulane; Villanova is next in Myrtle Beach Invitational |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2019/11/21/mississippi-state-cruises-past-tulane-villanova-next-myrtle-beach-invitational/4265322002/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=November 21, 2019}} As a freshman, he averaged 5.9 points per game. He missed the first three games of his sophomore season after testing positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].{{cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=Joel |title=Iverson Molinar's return expected to boost Bulldogs as Mississippi State gets set to host North Texas |url=https://www.si.com/college/mississippistate/basketball/molinar-return-msu-nt-12320 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=December 3, 2020}} On January 9, 2021, Molinar recorded 24 points, eight rebounds and four steals in an 84–81 victory over [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]]. He was subsequently named [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Player of the Week.{{cite web |last1=Middleton |first1=Dalton |title=MSU's Molinar named SEC Player of the Week |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/college/msus-molinar-named-sec-player-of-the-week/article_2839c2a1-0673-54ec-9dee-ed656f3f54a3.html |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]] |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=January 11, 2021}} As a sophomore, Molinar averaged 16.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=O'Connell |first1=Robert |title=Panamanians Division 1 players stats last season |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Panama/news/682850/Panamanians-Division-1-players-stats-last-season. |website=Latinbasket |access-date=September 2, 2021 |date=May 6, 2021}} On January 12, 2022, Molinar scored 28 points in an 88–72 win against [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]].{{cite news |title=Molinar scores 28, MSU hands Georgia 5th loss in row 88-72 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364863 |access-date=January 13, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 12, 2022}} On January 25, 2022, he scored a career-high 30 points in an 82–74 overtime loss against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite news |title=No. 12 Kentucky needs OT to give Calipari his 800th win |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364888 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 25, 2022}} Molinar was named to the First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as a junior.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}} As a junior, he averaged 17.5 points, 3.6 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game. On March 25, 2022, Molinar declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Thompson |first=Khari |title=Mississippi State basketball's Iverson Molinar declares for 2022 NBA Draft |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2022/03/25/iverson-molinar-declares-nba-draft-mississippi-state-basketball/7168956001/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |access-date=April 29, 2022 |date=March 25, 2022}} He later signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility.{{cite web |last=Krajisnik |first=Stefan |title=Mississippi State basketball's Iverson Molinar signs with agent, foregoes eligibility |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mississippi-state-basketballs-iverson-molinar-011452984.html |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=April 29, 2022 |date=April 26, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Wisconsin Herd (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Molinar joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]] and on September 19, 2022, he signed with them.{{cite web|first=James|last=Foglio|title=Bucks sign guard Iverson Molinar to one-year, $1.02 million deal|url=https://www.basketballinsiders.com/news/bucks-sign-guard-iverson-molinar-to-one-year-1-02-million-deal/|website=BasketballInsiders.com|date=September 19, 2022|access-date=September 3, 2023}} However, he was waived the next day{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bucks Waive Iverson Molinar|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/09/bucks-waive-iverson-molinar.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 20, 2022|access-date=September 3, 2023}} and subsequently joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]], making the opening day roster.{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2022-23 Opening Day Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2022-23-opening-day-roster/n-5895537|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} After rejoining Milwaukee for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]], Molinar re-signed with the Bucks on September 2, 2023. However, he was waived on the same day.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bucks Sign, Waive Iverson Molinar|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/09/bucks-sign-waive-iverson-molinar.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 3, 2023|access-date=September 3, 2023}} On October 30, Molinar rejoined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCE 2023 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}} ===Mexico City Capitanes (2023–2024)=== On December 8, 2023, Molinar was traded to the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD RECEIVE RETURNING PLAYER RIGHTS TO THREE PLAYERS IN TRADE|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-receive-returning-player-rights-to-three-players-in-trade|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}} ===Ostioneros de Guaymas (2024)=== On April 26, 2024, Molinar signed with the [[Ostioneros de Guaymas (basketball)|Ostioneros de Guaymas]] of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Ostioneros de Guaymas Transactions|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/77/Mexican-CIBACOPA/team/986/Ostioneros-de-Guaymas/transactions/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=April 27, 2024}} ===Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2024-winter)=== On July 24, 2024, Molinar signed with [[Hapoel Be'er Sheva B.C.|Hapoel Be'er Sheva]] of the [[Israeli Premier League|Ligat HaAl]].{{cite ==National team career== Molinar played for Panama's junior national teams from the age of 10. He made his debut with the [[Panama men's national basketball team|senior national team]] at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]], averaging three points per game.{{cite web |title=Iverson Molinar (PAN)'s profile - FIBA Americup 2017 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/americup/2017/player/Iverson-Molinar |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=January 13, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] | 31 || 8 || 15.4 || '''.489''' || .371 || .768 || 1.0 || 1.3 || .3 || .1 || 5.9 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] | 30 || 29 || 32.6 || .478 || '''.436''' || .804 || '''3.7''' || 2.3 || .9 || .1 || 16.7 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] | '''34''' || '''34''' || '''34.1''' || .454 || .252 || '''.868''' || 3.1 || '''3.6''' || '''1.2''' || '''.4''' || '''17.5''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 95 || 71 || 27.5 || .468 || .346 || .831 || 2.6 || 2.4 || .8 || .2 || 13.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Molinar is the son of Leyza Jones and Manuel Molinar. He is named after [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] basketball player [[Allen Iverson]].
